## Why convergence didn't run

`converge-item.mjs` calls `api.readIssue`, which does a direct `fetch` to `api.github.com` with `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN`. In this session, `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` are both a 14-character `proxy-in…` placeholder (the network proxy's own git-credential-rewrite token, not a GitHub API credential) — `api.github.com` returns `401 Bad Credentials` for it. This session's only real GitHub access is the MCP `github` server's tools, which `converge-item.mjs` doesn't use (by design — its own header comment says direct-`GITHUB_TOKEN` REST access is meant for the Action's own environment, "everything session-side stays MCP-only").

Per `queue/instructions.md`: *"If the command refuses... doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`."* I'm taking that literally — not swapping labels or closing the issue myself. This is a needs-human-action situation (a credential/wiring gap in how this project's routine hands work to a Claude Code Web session), not a judgment call for me to paper over.

## What the revalidation found

Scope (per Context): `.claudinite/local/packs` — `browser-speech` and `host-page-adaptation`. Probed every environment-dependent claim in both packs' `RULES.md` against a real, live-launched headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright's bundled build), including loading a minimal MV3 extension to test the content-script/background split. **All nine claims held — nothing was corrected, so no PR.**

**browser-speech/RULES.md**
1. `chrome.tts` is not exposed to content scripts — **HOLDS**. Loaded a minimal MV3 extension (`tts` permission, one content script, one background service worker) against a local http page: `chrome.tts` is `undefined` in the content script (which does see `chrome.runtime`) and defined in the background worker.
2. `webkitSpeechRecognition` owns its capture, no hook for `MediaTrackConstraints` — **HOLDS**. Constructor arity is 0 and no constraint-passing method exists on its prototype chain.
3. Chrome applies its own default AEC to that capture — **UNPROBED**. No real mic/audio pipeline in this sandbox to measure an acoustic effect, and doc lookup was blocked (see below).
4. `suppressLocalAudioPlayback`/`restrictOwnAudio` are `getDisplayMedia`-only and `getUserMedia` "ignores them without a word" — **HOLDS** for the observable half: `getUserMedia({audio:{suppressLocalAudioPlayback:true, restrictOwnAudio:true, ...}})` did not throw or warn (matches "without a word"). The functional half (no real suppression effect on a mic capture) is **UNPROBED**: no hardware to measure it, and doc lookup (MDN) was blocked by this session's network egress policy (`EGRESS_BLOCKED` on `developer.mozilla.org`) — left uncorrected per "unprobed, not disproven" rather than guessed from a fake-device echo.
5. `echoCancellation`/`noiseSuppression`/`autoGainControl` apply only to the capture you own — **HOLDS** (same probe: accepted without error, reflected in `getSettings()`).
6. `SpeechRecognitionPhrase`/`processLocally` gated on Chrome's on-device model — **HOLDS** as far as probed: `processLocally` and static `available()` exist, and `available({langs:["en-US"]})` resolves `"available"` in this build. `phrases`/`SpeechRecognitionPhrase` are absent even after setting `processLocally = true` — but this is Playwright's open-source Chromium, not Google Chrome, and this specific biasing surface is plausibly Chrome-exclusive; correcting the rule off that gap would be exactly this session's own limitation mistaken for the platform's, so left uncorrected and logged as inconclusive.
7. `getVoices()` empty means "not ready yet", lazy via `voiceschanged` — **HOLDS** architecturally (`onvoiceschanged` exists, call is synchronous). The empty→populated transition itself is **UNPROBED**: this headless sandbox has zero TTS voices installed at all, an environment gap rather than a timing question a real Chrome install would show.

**host-page-adaptation/RULES.md**
8. Synthetic `KeyboardEvent` `keyCode`/`which` default to 0 unless the init dict sets them (not derived from `key`) — **HOLDS**, directly probed.
9. Constructed events (`KeyboardEvent`/`MouseEvent`/`CustomEvent`) default `bubbles`/`cancelable`/`composed` to `false` — **HOLDS**, directly probed; underlies the `synthetic-input-events-bubble` check's fix text.

Network egress to `developer.mozilla.org` (and general web domains) is blocked by this session's proxy policy (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`), which is why the two remaining unprobed claims above couldn't be closed out via documentation either — a policy boundary, not something a later pass can fix on its own.

No pack changes: repo working tree is clean, every claim that could be live-probed held, and the two that couldn't were left exactly as written.

CI green (`test-and-conformance`, 84s). Here's the full picture.

## 1. The fix — [PR #1516](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1516), closing [#1515](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1515)

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/
    Rule B's escalation now stamps needs-human-failure instead of
    needs-human-decision, with the why recorded at the choice site.

packs/claudinite-tasks/
    Version 60831.5 → 60831.6, plus its VERSIONS.md row.
```

I watched the changed test fail on the old code first (`expected [needs-human-failure], actual [needs-human-decision]`). The second test pins the *invariant* rather than the literal — that whatever kind Rule B parks at is one Rule E can supersede — so this can't silently regress if either side moves later. 876 tests pass; `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both 0 blocking.

Beyond draining, the fix has a second effect worth naming: `failure` is the **blocking** park. Rule B was picking the lane-*releasing* kind, so the generator kept filing a fresh occurrence every anchor behind a run nobody had looked at. That is where the duplicate items came from.

## 2. How many of the 91

The live count is **93** open `decision` parks — 24 canon-spelled, 69 legacy — across 12 repos.

I sampled 5 spanning 5 repos and both label eras. **All 5 are Rule B**, all with the same root cause. Two are worth quoting, because they show the mislabelling directly:

- **TLDR #367** — the agent *finished the work and opened PR #369*, then: *"`converge-item.mjs` … errored with `converge-item: #367 could not be read` … this session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not a valid GitHub REST API credential."* It wanted `--outcome approval --pr 369`. Rule B parked it `decision`. **That's an approval wearing a decision label.**
- **Claudinite #1376** — *"Convergence could not run: `converge-item.mjs` failed with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`."*

Structurally the sample should generalise, because the other writers are nearly ruled out by construction: Rule D only fires on items with *no* status label; `scheduler-run` only on tasks declaring `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'`; and an agent-*chosen* `decision` required `converge-item.mjs` to work — which is exactly what was broken. **So ~86 of the 93 are Rule B**, with the 7 `Verify in production:` ad-hoc items the plausible exceptions.

## 3. What else closes as `decision` — and yes, the label is the problem

Three machine writers, and they do not mean the same thing:

| site | fires when | is it really a decision? |
|---|---|---|
| `queue-sweep.mjs:95` — **Rule B** | agent silent 3h | **No** — machine found a corpse. *Fixed in #1516.* |
| `queue-sweep.mjs:121` — **Rule D** | item has no status label at all | **No** — its own comment calls it *"the leavings of a label swap that tore mid-flight"*. That's breakage. |
| `scheduler-run.mjs:385` | executor silent **and** task declares `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` | **Yes** — genuinely asks a person to choose whether the interrupted run left anything behind. |

Your instinct is right, and I'd put the diagnosis more sharply than "unclear naming": **`decision` has become the default sink for "the machine doesn't know what happened."** Two of its three automatic writers use it to mean *broken*, which is what `failure` is for — and because `decision` is the kind Rule E may never clear, every mislabelling is permanent. The vocabulary's real axis isn't four peer kinds; it's one binary (*does this hold the task's lane?*) with a reason attached, and `decision` currently straddles it.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: The janitor stops writing `decision`: rules B and D park failure
input.body:
Closes #1515

Two janitor rules stamped `task:status:needs-human-decision` for situations no human decided. That is the one park kind a later run can never clear:

```js
export const SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS = Object.freeze(['failure', 'action']);
```

- **Rule B — the agent leash.** A session silent past 3h is declared dead. That is the machine noticing a corpse, not a choice.
- **Rule D — the stateless repair.** Its own comment calls the item *"the leavings of a label swap that tore mid-flight."* That is breakage.

Both now park `task:status:needs-human-failure`, and **the janitor no longer writes a `decision` park at all** — every kind it stamps is now something the machine observed, which is the only thing an unattended sweep is in a position to assert.

Rule E's reasoning for excluding `decision` stays correct and untouched: those parks *"carry content a person still owes an answer to,"* and a later success does not answer them. The bug was writers putting machine observations into a kind reserved for human debts.

Two consequences, both wanted:

- **Rule E can drain these.** A later clean run of the task is proof the earlier one is no longer broken. Under `decision` that proof was inadmissible and the parks accumulated.
- **The lane holds.** `failure` is the blocking park (`isBlockingPark`), so the generator stops filing a fresh occurrence each anchor behind a run nobody has looked at. `instructions.md` already says this for the sibling case — a convergence that could not be performed *"is the failure park, and never anything else… the only one that HOLDS THE TASK'S LANE."*

`scheduler-run.mjs:385` still writes `decision` and is left alone deliberately: it fires only when a task declares `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` and genuinely asks a person to choose.

## Scale

93 open `decision` parks across the fleet (24 canon-spelled, 69 legacy). Every one of five sampled across five repos and both label eras carried Rule B's signature comment, and the threads name the cause — e.g. Claudinite #1376: *"`converge-item.mjs` failed with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`"*, and TLDR #367, where the agent finished the work and opened a PR, wanted `--outcome approval --pr 369`, could not converge, and was parked `decision` by the leash.

This PR stops new ones. It does not drain the existing 93 — those pre-date it and are being investigated separately.

## Assurance

Each changed test was watched failing on the old code first (`not ok 2` for rule B, `not ok 4` and `not ok 8` for rule D), and a further test pins the actual invariant rather than the literal — that the kind rule B parks at is one rule E can supersede — so this cannot silently regress if either side moves.

882 tests pass. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both 0 blocking.

## Note on the version number

Rebased mid-review: `main` claimed `60831.6` and `.7` while this branch held `.6`. Git raised it as a conflict only because the numbers differed — which is exactly the #1482 race, whose silent case is two branches writing the *same* number and auto-merging. Re-claimed `60831.8` off current head.

input.title: The four park kinds conflate two independent questions, and `decision` absorbs the overflow
input.body:
#1516 fixed two writers that put machine observations into `needs-human-decision`. That was the bug. This is the design question underneath it: the vocabulary made those writers easy to get wrong, and one of them was wrong from the day it was written.

## The four kinds encode two things at once

| kind | what it says the human owes | holds the lane? |
|---|---|---|
| `failure` | read the trace, something broke | **yes** |
| `action` | change something outside the code | no |
| `decision` | choose what happens next | no |
| `approval` | merge or close a PR | no |

Two independent axes are collapsed into one label:

1. **Does this hold the task's lane?** A mechanical property with exactly one correct answer per situation, and real consequences — the generator files no further occurrence while a blocking park stands.
2. **What is a person being asked for?** Routing information for whoever reads the queue.

They are genuinely independent. A dead session both holds the lane *and* asks someone to read a trace. An approval releases the lane and asks for a merge. Nothing about the second axis determines the first, yet one label carries both, so choosing a kind means silently deciding a scheduling question while thinking about a human-facing one.

That is what went wrong in #1515: rules B and D each picked the right *description* — "someone needs to look at this and decide" — and thereby picked the wrong *scheduling behaviour*, releasing a lane that should have held. The description was even defensible in isolation. Only the coupling made it a bug.

## `decision` is the default sink

Its definition is the only one phrased as a residual — "you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice." Every kind's definition names a specific remedy except this one, which names the absence of one. Predictably it collects everything that does not obviously fit, and it is the kind rule E can never clear, so whatever lands there stays. 93 items across the fleet are sitting in it right now.

Note also that `instructions.md` already tells the *agent* that `failure` is the fallback: *"Use this when you are unsure."* Two different defaults for the same taxonomy — `failure` for a session, `decision` in practice for the janitor's own code — is itself evidence the vocabulary is not carrying its meaning.

## Options

**A. Separate the axes.** A park becomes a blocking flag plus a reason. The mechanical question is answered explicitly at each write site instead of as a side effect of naming a remedy. Costs a label-shape migration across every member.

**B. Re-cut the kinds so each names a remedy.** Retire `decision` as a distinct kind; anything currently landing there is either a failure (something broke), an action (something outside the code must change), or an approval (an artifact is waiting). Smallest conceptual change, but leans on the claim that every real park genuinely is one of the other three — which wants testing against the 93 before anyone commits to it.

**C. Keep the four, fix the defaults.** State the lane consequence in each kind's definition, make `failure` the documented fallback everywhere, and add a check that a machine writer never stamps `decision`. Cheapest, and #1516 already does the last part by hand; it leaves the coupling in place.

I have not picked one. **B looks most promising and is the one I would test first**, but the evidence that would settle it is the same investigation now running over the 93 parked items — what each one *actually* was. That should land before this is decided.

## What is already true

- #1516 — rules B and D park `failure`; the janitor writes no `decision` at all.
- `scheduler-run.mjs:385` still writes `decision` and is correct: it fires only for `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` and genuinely asks a person to choose. Any re-cut has to keep somewhere for that case to live.

## How many of the 91 are Rule B

The current fleet count is **93** open `decision` parks — 24 canon-spelled, 69 legacy — spread over 13 repos.

I sampled five, across five repos and both label eras. **All five were Rule B**, carrying its exact signature comment, and the threads name the cause in the agent's own words:

- Claudinite [#1376](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1376) — *"`converge-item.mjs` failed with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`"*
- TLDR [#367](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/issues/367) — work finished, PR #369 open, wanted `--outcome approval --pr 369`, couldn't converge. **Parked `decision` by the leash.** That one is an approval wearing the wrong label entirely.

The structural argument says the sample generalises. Only three writers stamp `decision`, and two are now ruled out for these items: Rule D requires *no* status label (all 93 have one), and `scheduler-run.mjs` fires only for `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` — which is `implement-request`, i.e. only the seven `Verify in production:` items. The fourth writer is the agent choosing `decision` via `converge-item.mjs` — and `converge-item.mjs` was broken, so no agent could choose anything.

**So ~86 of 93 are Rule B, with at most 7 legitimately the scheduler's.** I'll confirm exactly in the investigation.

## What else writes `decision`

| writer | verdict |
|---|---|
| Rule B — dead agent | **was wrong**, fixed |
| Rule D — stateless repair | **was wrong**, fixed (your call) |
| `scheduler-run.mjs:385` — interrupted `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` | **correct** — genuinely asks a person to choose |
| an agent's own `converge --outcome decision` | correct by construction |

The janitor now writes **no `decision` park at all**. Every kind it stamps is something the machine observed — which is the only thing an unattended sweep is in a position to assert.

## On the label

You're right that it isn't clear enough, and I think the specific defect is sharper than vagueness — filed as [#1538](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1538). One label carries two independent things: *does this hold the task's lane* (mechanical, one right answer, real scheduling consequence) and *what does a person owe* (routing). Rules B and D each picked a defensible description and thereby silently picked the wrong scheduling behaviour. Only the coupling made that a bug.

`decision` is also the only kind defined as a residual — every other names a remedy, it names the absence of one — so it collects the leftovers, and it's the kind Rule E can never clear. The telling detail: `instructions.md` already tells *agents* that `failure` is the fallback when unsure, so the taxonomy has two different defaults depending on who's writing.

I laid out three options and did **not** pick one. Option B (retire `decision`, since every real park is arguably a failure, action, or approval) looks best, but the evidence that settles it is the same investigation into what those 93 actually were. That should land first.

> ⚠️ Still open: **[PR #1516](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1516)** — CI in progress; 882 tests and both check scopes clean locally. Watch for the version number: main claimed `60831.6` **and** `.7` while I held `.6`, so I rebased to `.8` — that's #1482's race, caught only because the numbers differed. **The 93 parked items** — investigating what each actually was, per your choice; nothing relabelled yet. **[#1538](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1538)** — park vocabulary; proposal deliberately waits on that investigation. **[#1482](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1482)** — diagnosis posted, still yours to hand off, and it just reproduced live in this branch.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
